note: Collectibles and seats. Every spot is relative to a plot, an annex or the path of its island, never a world coordinate, so a new layout carries them along. Colours name a key of PALETTE in src/config/00-config.js. topic is a tech tree id in vibemap/tech.py.

items.name: A commit
items.concept: A commit is a labelled save point in your work that you can always return to.

items.name: A pull request
items.concept: A pull request is a branch asking to join the main line, with the review attached.

items.name: A token
items.concept: A model reads and writes tokens, the word pieces you are billed for.

items.name: A container
items.concept: A container ships the machine together with the program, so it runs the same everywhere.

items.name: A packet
items.concept: Everything you send over a network travels as small addressed packets that are put back together at the other end.

items.name: A key
items.concept: A key proves who you are to a server without ever sending your password.

items.name: A test tube
items.concept: A test is a question with a known answer, asked again after every change.

items.name: A coffee bean
items.concept: Every agent run costs money per token, so measure a small run before you scale it.

items.name: A scroll of YAML
items.concept: YAML is the indented list of settings that pipelines, containers and agents read.

items.name: A prompt
items.concept: A prompt with a scope, a keep list and a do not touch list is most of the craft.

items.name: A version tag
items.concept: A version number tells you whether an upgrade can break you: major breaks, minor adds, patch fixes.

items.name: A git hook
items.concept: A git hook is a script git runs for you at commit or push time, so the rule cannot be forgotten.

items.name: A note
items.concept: Markdown is plain text with a few marks, which is why it still opens in thirty years.

items.name: A table
items.concept: SQL asks a question of a table and gets rows back, with no loop to write.

items.name: An API call
items.concept: An API is a promise about the shape of the answer, so two programs can agree without meeting.

items.name: An environment variable
items.concept: An environment variable keeps a secret out of your code and inside the machine that runs it.

items.name: A pipeline run
items.concept: Continuous integration runs your checks on someone else's machine on every push, so green means green.

items.name: A frozen row
items.concept: Data at rest is cheap and data in motion is expensive, which is the whole reason cold storage exists.

items.name: A TOML file
items.concept: TOML is configuration written for people to read, with sections and plain keys.

items.name: A context window
items.concept: The context window is everything the model can see at once, and it is smaller than your repository.

items.name: A changelog entry
items.concept: A changelog is the human half of the history, written for the people who have to upgrade.

items.name: A decision record
items.concept: A decision record says what was chosen and why, so the next person does not reopen it from scratch.

items.name: A vault note
items.concept: A note becomes knowledge the moment you link it to another note.

items.name: A rented server
items.concept: The cloud is a computer you rent by the hour and never see, billed while you forget about it.

items.name: Localhost
items.concept: Localhost is your own machine answering itself, on a port you picked.

items.name: A dotfile
items.concept: A dotfile is your tool remembering how you like it, saved where you can copy it to the next machine.

items.name: A Python script
items.concept: Python is the language most of this stack is written in, and twenty lines of it replace an afternoon.

items.name: A file path
items.concept: A path is an address, and everything else in the terminal is a verb applied to one.

items.name: A config file
items.concept: Configuration is the part of a program you are allowed to change without reading the code.

items.name: A structured prompt
items.concept: A prompt reads best as role, task, constraints and the shape of the answer you want back.

items.name: A secret vault
items.concept: A secret belongs in a vault or a keychain, never in the repository, not even briefly.

items.name: An agent hook
items.concept: An agent hook runs your own command around a tool call, which is how you keep an agent inside the lines.

items.name: A subagent
items.concept: A subagent gets its own context and hands back only the answer, which keeps the main thread clean.

items.name: A cluster
items.concept: Kubernetes keeps a stated number of containers alive, and most projects never need it.

items.name: An MCP server
items.concept: MCP is one plug shape for tools, so a model can use a service nobody wrote a custom client for.

items.name: An SSH key
items.concept: SSH gives you a shell on another machine over an encrypted link, with a key instead of a password.

items.name: A harness
items.concept: The harness is the loop around the model: your files, your tools and your rules.

items.name: A headless run
items.concept: Headless means the agent runs without you in the room, on a schedule or on an event.

items.name: An AGENTS.md
items.concept: AGENTS.md is the file every agent reads first, and it is the cheapest way to be understood.

items.name: A skill
items.concept: A skill is a folder of instructions an agent loads only when the task matches.
